input:
Boot fails after an OTA update that included a new PMIC firmware blob. The device gets stuck at the PMIC init stage. U-Boot log (captured via UART):

  [PMIC] mt6363: probe start
  [PMIC] mt6363: reading HWCID... 0x63
  [PMIC] mt6363: sending LDO_VAUD18 enable seq
  [PMIC] mt6363: LDO_VAUD18 timeout: expected ready in 500us, waited 2ms
  [PMIC] mt6363: BUCK_VCORE power-good timeout (PGOOD=0 after 5ms)
  [PMIC] ERROR: voltage sequencing failure, halting
  [WDT] System watchdog expired, issuing reset

The OTA diff changed `/vendor/firmware/mt6363.bin` from v2.1.3 to v2.2.0. In the old firmware, LDO_VAUD18 enables before BUCK_VCORE, which is correct for our board. The new firmware appears to have reordered the voltage ramp sequence. Is this a PMIC firmware ordering regression or a board-level power sequencing constraint violation? What is the safest way to bisect the PMIC firmware change and confirm which sequence step is causing BUCK_VCORE PGOOD to fail?
